To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the GLEAMS model simulated P losses in surface and sub-surface runoff and NO3 losses in leachate reasonably well, but the model overestimated NH4-N losses in runoff and underestimated P losses in subsurface runoff.
the GLEAMS model simulated nutrient (N andP) losses in surface runoff but not in subsurface runoff.
GLEAMS (2.1) was not able to simulate P losses in runoff and leachate and N transformation processes in the soil.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: (1) the application of a model to predict the nutrient losses from the application of poultry litter; (2) the comparison of the model results with the field data; and (3) the modification of the model to improve the simulation of the nutrient losses from poultry litter.
the application of the GLEAMS model to predict the fate of P and N from land application of two rates of poultry litter and one rate of commercial fertilizer.
the application of GLEAMS (version 2) to predict the losses of nutrients in surface runoff and leachate from a corn field following the application of poultry litter and commercial fertilizers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the model did not simulate N and P losses in runoff and leachate from the poultry-litter-amended corn plots as well as it did from the fertilizer-amended plots.
the GLEAMS model is not yet suitable for predicting nutrient losses from land applications of poultry litter.
GLEAMS was not able to simulate N and P losses from poultry litter and commercial fertilizer in the surface runoff and leachate in a manner consistent with field observations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GLEAMS model is not adequate for predicting nutrient losses in surface runoff from poultry litter applications.
the GLEAMS model did not simulate the nutrient dynamics of poultry litter application on conventionally tilling corn.
the GLEAMS simulation did not agree with the observed field data for the N and P losses in runoff and leachate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the GLEAMS model is not appropriate for predicting nutrient losses in runoff and leachate after poultry litter applications.
the GLEAMS model is not capable of predicting nutrient losses from application of poultry litter on conventionally tilling soil.
the GLEAMS model is a good tool for simulating N losses from land application and management practices.
